newsitem.title: USA: Amphenol to be bought by KKR affiliate.
newsitem.headline: Amphenol to be bought by KKR affiliate.

text.p: Amphenol Corp said Thursday it had agreed to be acquired by NXS Acquisition Corp, an affiliate of Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co (KKR), in a deal worth $1.5 billion including refinanced debt.
The transaction will leave the KKR affiliate with over 75 percent of Amphenol, which will retain its New York Stock Exchange listing.
The terms are $26 cash per share. Up to 10 percent of Amphenol stock, or 4.4 million shares, can be retained by present shareholders.
If shares elected to be retained exceed 4.4 million, then those shares available will be pro-rated among those electing to retain shares and the balance paid in cash.
If retentions are less than 4.4 million shares, then remaining shares will be prorated among those electing cash.
Lawrence DeGeorge, Amphenol chairman, his family and an associated trust with a total 30 percent of Amphenol's outstanding shares have agreed to vote in favor of the deal, Amphenol said.
KKR, through affiliates, will invest up to $374 million in the transaction, while the balance of the $1.5 billion will come from bank or subordinated debt, a spokeswoman said.
Amphenol, which makes cables and connectors for electronic and industrial applications, has 44.7 million shares outstanding, valued by the deal at $1.16 billion.
The deal includes refinancing over $300 million of Amphenol debt.
"I am enthusiastic about the opportunity being created for the future develpoment of Amphenol by this transaction," said Martin Loeffler, Amphenol chief executive.

"KKR's financial resources and expertise provide strong support for the company as it pursues new development programs, acquisitions and investments to capitalize on and further expand its worldwide presence," Loeffler said.

The deal provisions exclude Amphenol from soliciting another merger deal. An affiliate of KKR can under some circumstances call the DeGeorge family stock at $26 per share, and following the recapitalization they will have the option to sell any retained shares to the KKR affiliate at $26 each.
Amphenol will continue to be run by current management at its Connecticut headquarters. The deal is subject to shareholder approval and financing finalization.
